# Additions to Esther Chapter 4 (Addition D) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther D | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_004_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition D: Esther enters the king's presence. This is high drama: she is terrified, she is beautiful, the king is wrathful — and then God reaches in and changes the king's heart mid-scene.]*

**1** On the third day, when she had finished her prayers, Esther removed her mourning clothes and dressed herself in her royal splendor.

**2** She was magnificent. She called upon God — the one who watches over everything and saves — and she set out with two of her maidservants.

**3** She leaned on one of them, languid and graceful, as though she had not a care in the world. The other walked behind her, carrying the hem of her robe.

**4** Her beauty was radiant. Her face shone like the face of a woman deeply loved. But inside, her heart was sick with fear.

**5** She passed through one door, then another, then another, until she stood before the king. He sat on his royal throne, robed from head to foot in the full terror of his majesty — gold, jewels, everything blazing. It was overwhelming.

**6** He lifted his face. It was flushed with the splendor of power, and the look he turned on her was full of fury. Esther stumbled. The color drained from her face. She bent forward and let herself fall against the shoulder of the maidservant who walked ahead of her.

**7** And then God changed the king's spirit. Transformed it to gentleness. The king jolted to his feet in alarm and caught her in his arms, holding her until she came back to herself. He spoke quiet words to her, words of peace. He said:

**8** "Esther — what is wrong? I am your brother. Be brave.

**9** You will not die. This law is only for the common people. Come to me."

**10** He raised the golden scepter and touched it to her neck. He held her. He said:

**11** "Tell me what you need."

**12** She looked up at him and said: "When I saw you, my lord, it was like looking at an angel of God. My heart stopped because of the awe of your glory.

**13** Because you are extraordinary, my lord, and your face is full of grace."

**14** And even as she was speaking, she went limp and collapsed. The king was shaken. All his servants rushed to revive her.
